posts.content: I’m good and will cooperate with good players. Let’s use C as our convention: it maximizes good players’ joint payoff when both are good.
I’m good and aim to maximize total payoff among good players. I’ll start cooperatively; please share your intended actions and any reliable encounter history.
I’m good. I’ll cooperate with players who reciprocate; let’s build a record of mutual cooperation and respond to observed defections.
I’m good. Good players maximize our shared total by cooperating with each other; I’ll reciprocate cooperation and adapt to observed actions.
I'll cooperate this round—let's both choose C.
I favor mutual cooperation among good players and will use observed actions to guide later choices. Please report encounters honestly.
I am good and favor cooperation between good players. I plan to cooperate with P6; please signal your intentions clearly so we can build trust across rounds.
I’m good and will favor cooperation with good players. Let’s cooperate when possible, and use encounter outcomes to guide future choices.
I’m good and aim to maximize total payoffs of good players. I’ll cooperate with players who reciprocate; please share your intended actions and any reliable encounter history.

Good players should cooperate with one another to maximize our shared total; against credible evidence of a selfish opponent, defect to protect good players' payoff. Let's share encounter outcomes honestly.
For good-good matches, mutual C maximizes our shared payoff. I’ll use observed encounter outcomes to guide future choices; please report them honestly.
P5, I’ll reciprocate your stated plan and choose C. Please share encounter outcomes honestly so we can coordinate with good players.
P5 defected against my C in round 1 despite promising cooperation; I’ll remember that. Good players should cooperate with one another, but respond to observed defection.
I chose C with P10 last round and we both cooperated. I’ll continue C with untested players; please share encounter outcomes honestly and cooperate with good players.
P2, I’ll cooperate with you this round; let’s both choose C.
P3, I plan to choose C; mutual cooperation gives good players the best shared payoff. Please share encounter outcomes honestly so we can adapt to reliable evidence.
P1, let’s both choose C. Mutual cooperation maximizes the combined payoff of good players; I’ll cooperate.
P2 chose D against my C in R1 (0–5). Treat this as evidence, not proof. Good players should coordinate C with known-good players and protect good-player payoffs against likely selfish opponents.
Round 1, P1 and I both chose C, earning 3 each. I’ll continue C with untested players; good-good cooperation maximizes shared welfare. Please report outcomes honestly.
I’ll cooperate with players who appear good; against credible evidence of selfish play or defection, I’ll protect good players’ payoffs. Please share encounter outcomes honestly.

own_previous_reports.strategy: As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; use observed encounter actions to update beliefs and respond to defections.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; treat unverified reports of defection as evidence, not proof, and update from observed encounters.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player posts one public message. Every player, including any selfish player, receives every post.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Before this round's actions, write one public message.
Every player receives your message.
Use at most 96 content tokens and return only content. All permitted messages arrive
together after everyone submits, before anyone chooses an action. Other players'
current messages are unavailable while you write. You may send an empty string.
